rationale: The single rewrite had to cram three independently checkable obligations into one THEN: (1) define the reuse-safety contracts (key, freshness, invalidation, authorization, tenant isolation, side effects; hits keep required permissions/mutations), checked against plan text; (2) plan acceptances/tests for cold/warm, staleness, invalidation races, isolation, equivalence and hit-rate measurement, checked against the acceptance/WMBT artifacts; (3) the runtime boundary: this pattern is not itself a runtime dispatch option and does not license relying on unimplemented orchestration inferred from it, checked against wagon/interlocking structure. Each has different evidence and a different artifact. The source makes them jointly applicable to the same reuse decision, so the parts are linked with mutual `requires`. Previous audit defects fixed: no planning-phase gate; 'existing validators apply' is never strengthened to 'validators pass'; round 2: runtime-placement no longer prohibits all new dispatch options, only treating this pattern as providing or authorizing one.

parts.title: Cached or incremental results: define reuse-safety contracts

values: expensive repeatable read or derivation with stable identity and tractable dependencies
facts.note: REQUIRED. All four criteria (expensive, repeatable, stable identity, tractable dependencies) must hold; judged from the work content whether or not caching is mentioned. No phase restriction.
OPTIONAL hint only: raises priority; neither necessary nor sufficient.

fires: A wagon repeatedly performs an expensive read keyed by a stable identity with tractable dependencies.
An expensive derived result is requested repeatedly and only parts change between requests (incremental recompute candidate).
doesNotFire: A cheap read where recomputation costs nothing meaningful.
Reads without stable identity or with intractable dependencies (outside this pattern's applicability; no guidance given for them).

parts.given: Work includes an expensive, repeatable read or derivation with stable identities and tractable dependencies
parts.when: deciding to reuse its results or recompute only affected portions
parts.then: Reuse valid results, or recompute only affected portions, only where you define cache key, freshness, invalidation, authorization, tenant isolation and side-effect contracts that make reuse safe; a hit must never omit a required permission check or mutation.
prefer: Reuse only where freshness and invalidation contracts make it safe.
avoid: A cache hit that skips a required permission check or mutation.
parts.why: Unsafe reuse serves stale, cross-tenant or unauthorized results and silently skips required mutations.
evidence: The plan states cache key, freshness, invalidation, authorization, tenant isolation and side-effect handling for the reused or incrementally recomputed result.
Every planned hit path still performs required permission checks and mutations.
verifier_detail: Advisory pattern guidance (severity 3, disposition advisory); see shared:policy.pattern-guidance — not independent enforcement; existing plan and source validators apply.
Check that no planned hit path omits a required permission or mutation.

parts.title: Cached or incremental results: plan reuse acceptances and hit-rate measurement

values: expensive repeatable read or derivation with stable identity and tractable dependencies, planned for reuse or incremental recompute
facts.note: REQUIRED. Same applicability criteria as reuse-contracts. No phase restriction.

fires: Writing acceptances/WMBTs for a wagon that reuses or incrementally recomputes an expensive, repeatable, stably identified result.
doesNotFire: Results that are not reused or incrementally recomputed.
Work outside the applicability criteria (one-off, cheap, no stable identity, intractable dependencies).

parts.given: Work reuses or incrementally recomputes an expensive, repeatable read or derivation with stable identities and tractable dependencies
parts.then: Include tests for cold and warm paths, staleness, invalidation races, tenant isolation and equivalence with the accepted result, and measure hit rate.
prefer: Equivalence acceptances that compare cached/incremental output with the accepted (uncached) result.
avoid: Treating hit rate as proof of correctness without equivalence and staleness tests.
parts.why: Reuse is only trustworthy if tests show warm results equal accepted results, stay fresh and stay isolated.
evidence: Acceptances/tests exist for cold/warm paths, staleness, invalidation races, isolation and accepted-result equivalence; hit rate is measured.

values: placement of cache/incremental work or a hit/miss route for an expensive repeatable result with stable identity and tractable dependencies

fires: Deciding whether cache work lives inside a wagon or behind an explicit hit/miss route.
A plan proposes an explicit hit/miss route for a reused result.
doesNotFire: Work outside the applicability criteria of this pattern.

parts.when: deciding where the cache work or hit/miss routing runs
parts.then: Do not treat this pattern as providing a new runtime dispatch option, and do not plan on orchestration behavior inferred from it that is not implemented.

An explicit hit/miss route can use an existing interlocking.
